newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber steady to lower despite govt buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber steady to lower despite govt buying.

text.p: The Thai government's purchase of 7,000 tonnes of rubber this week barely lifted local prices as external demand was flat, trade sources said on Wednesday.
But news that the govenment intended to buy more rubber to shore up prices gave the market some hope that prices would be at least supported around current levels.

Benchmark RSS3 rubber for May delivery was quoted around 123 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok compared with 123-124 cents on Friday. Concentrated latex was quoted around 93 cents on the same basis, unchanged from last week.
The government on Tuesday bought 7,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade for 123.5 cents a kg after negotiating for that price since Friday, a source at Hat Yai auction market told Reuters.
"Except for that deal, there was almost no activity in the market. We were just dying for orders," said on Hat Yai-based trader.
A senior agriculture ministry official told Reuters on Wednesday that the government had bought 26,400 tonnes of sheet rubber so far since March 5 to prop up prices.
